transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-14 09:30 PDT
Duration: ~68 minutes
Attendees: Maya, Liam, Priya, Diego, Hannah

Summary (auto): quick decision lab; tradeoffs between quant profiles and rollback complexity; finalize telemetry for canary.

00:00 Maya: alright, let's get started, thanks everyone for carving out an hour. we wanted to run a focused lab today — decide the acceptable quality delta for 8-bit and 4-bit quant, and define fallback triggers for hosted and dedicated fleets.
00:18 Liam: I'll kick off with the current numbers — on the staging cluster we saw median latency improvements of 30% with 8-bit, 58% with 4-bit, but quality drift is noisy, especially on instruction-following prompts.
00:34 Diego: yeah and to add, the kv-cache behavior for long contexts w/ 4-bit shows token-lag on certain kernels; might be an implementation artifact or quant rounding.
00:47 Hannah: i've got some quick evals — 20 prompts across safety, code, and multi-turn. 8-bit is usually within 2-3% metric delta on our rouge/bertscore proxy, 4-bit can jump to 8-12% in worst cases.
01:02 Priya: so operationally, is 8-bit a safe default for hosted? what about Dedicated where customers expect low variance?
01:11 Maya: that's the key question. my bias is make 8-bit default for hosted with telemetry and a soft gate for dedicated — require customer opt-in after a brief pilot.
01:24 Liam: can we be more prescriptive: define "soft gate" as run canary at 1% traffic for 72 hours, if quality-regression > 4% on our eval set or error-rate > 0.5% then roll back automatically.
01:41 Diego: automated rollback on quality is tricky — we need robust metrics, not just a single metric — per-intent breakdown and prompt-level regression alerts. otherwise we get noisy flips.
01:55 Hannah: agree. we should have prompt-level buckets and use median + 90th percentile to decide. a 4% overall might hide a 15% regression on a critical intent.
02:10 Priya: from SRE side, we also want latency/cpu/gpu-mem signals. 4-bit can reduce GPU memory pressure and increase concurrency; if we see latency tail increase while GPU is saturated that's suspicious.
02:25 Liam: add invariants: if p95 latency increases by >15% AND av mem reduce > 20% then flag. but the primary rollback should be quality not latency.
02:38 Maya: let's try to codify a decision matrix live:
 - 8-bit hosted: default on after canary; rollback if eval gross delta > 4% OR prompt-level regress > 8% on critical intents OR error-rate > 0.5%
 - 4-bit hosted: pilot only; require manual approval and extended canary 5 days, rollback if gross delta > 6% or prompt-level regress > 12%
 - Dedicated: always opt-in, customer must sign off on quant profile; for enterprise accounts we can surface tradeoffs in Console.
03:05 Diego: technical note: some models use per-channel quant scales which are more robust; we should prefer per-channel 8-bit and only use per-tensor 4-bit when memory constrained. that nuance should be in the docs.
03:24 Hannah: do we have a way to tag model variants in the catalog so routing respects quant profile? we'll need that for canary and fallback.
03:33 Liam: yes, model-variant tags exist, but routing policies need one more flag to prefer "quality-first" vs "cost-first". implement quick toggle on canary route.
03:43 Priya: on observability — what dashboards do we need? i propose: a) eval-rubric dashboard with per-intent delta b) prompt-level regression scatter c) system metrics overlay (latency, gpu-mem). plus a binary canary flag and timeframe.
03:58 Diego: and perf heatmap by sequence-length; quant skew seems worse for long seqs. add a KV-cache hit-rate layer.
04:12 Hannah: one annoyance — our current eval harness sometimes mislabels model names in the logs, so linking eval deltas to the exact variant can be brittle. we should standardize variant_id in the pipeline.
04:25 Maya: action item: Diego to run a cross-model quant-skew matrix (FP16 vs 8-bit vs 4-bit) and upload spreadsheet. include per-prompt diffs and p95 tail metrics.
04:36 Diego: noted. will include per-architecture rows (gpt-like / seq2seq / code).
04:44 Priya: PagerDuty/alerting: we'll need composite alerts — e.g., eval-delta > threshold AND traffic > X => page. Otherwise we get paged for noise during low traffic.
04:57 Liam: also need a fallback chain: first route to 8-bit variant, then to full-precision default model, then to a smaller but higher-quality model if needed. define max failover hops = 2.
05:11 Maya: ok, let's role-play a failure scenario: canary shows 6% gross regression on critical-intent for 8-bit at 48h. What happens?
05:20 Diego: automated rollback to FP16 variant for affected route; fill incident ticket, notify AE/customer-facing team, hold traffic for 2 hours and monitor.
05:31 Priya: and if rollback fails (e.g., incompatible kernels), fallback to regional replica that hasn't been updated. but that's messy; we should try to avoid kernel mismatches via coordinated deploys.
05:44 Hannah: decision on metrics: use our rubric (coherence, instruction-following, hallucination proxy). weight critical-intent more. that's in the rubric doc link: https://redwood.internal/docs/quant-rubric (note: internal doc).
05:58 Maya: for canaries, who owns the sign-off? suggestion: Diego to run data + Hannah to score + Maya to approve.
06:08 Liam: logging detail: store per-request quality score in trace logs for sampled requests, keep 7d retention for canary analysis. that's expensive but worth it for short canaries.
06:20 Priya: on cost: we have to estimate dollars saved vs risk. 8-bit saves ~23% token-cost on average in our recent run; 4-bit saves ~40% but risk is higher. include that in the pilot brief.
06:33 Diego: technical gotcha — some tensors are latency-sensitive and quantizing them increases compute time due to dequantize ops. We'll profile which layers are net-win.
06:45 Hannah: question from the back: what about private deployments / private control plane — will customers want 4-bit inside their VPC?
06:53 Maya: our stance: private = customer choice. we will surface the quant recommendations, but require explicit opt-in for non-default quant profiles. also include a warning and a support SLA adjustment.
07:06 Liam: another operational requirement: the Console needs a per-route "canary window" and a one-click rollback button that ties into the same policy engine. Otherwise triage is too manual.
07:22 Priya: runbook sketch:
 - detect: eval delta + traffic threshold
 - validate: run quick re-eval on sampled prompts
 - action: automatic rollback if validated OR alert ops for manual decision
 - postmortem: generate auto report with sample prompts and diff snapshots
07:40 Diego: anything on quant-aware kernel selection? we should tag kernels that are validated for quantized runtimes and fail deployment if not validated. reduces mismatch risk.
07:52 Hannah: noted — add kernel-validation pipeline to CI.
07:59 Maya: ok let's go around for clarifying questions and owners.
08:05 Liam: i want to ensure the thresholds are conservative for first two pilots; we can loosen after N successful runs. proposal: start with 4% gross for 8-bit, tighten to 3% after 3 successful canaries. agreed?
08:18 Hannah: agreed. also add an explicit check for hallucination metric; if hallucination proxy increases > 2% on critical intents, immediate rollback.
08:29 Priya: i'll add composite pager rule: eval delta > threshold AND sampled traffic > 500 reqs/hour => page. otherwise create ticket.
08:40 Diego: will add per-architecture rows and include kernel compatibility notes in the spreadsheet.
08:47 Maya: last item: communication plan. if pilot fails, we notify customer success and optionally offer extended FP16 capacity while we remediate. if pilot succeeds, we put a note in the release notes and flag customers who opted into quant gains.
08:59 Hannah: weird transcription note: some names in the eval harness show up as "speaker 7" — we'll fix mapping.
09:06 Maya: okay great. to recap: owners and due dates as in action items. Diego, Hannah, Priya, Maya. we'll reconvene after Diego uploads the matrix and Hannah finishes the rubric.
09:19 Liam: any objections? none heard.
09:22 Maya: thanks everyone, meeting adjourned.
